comparator.sourceNotes: The official year pages supply 60+60+60=180 EC. The first year comprises 11 compulsory religious-studies courses totaling 60 EC, excluding zero-credit Instruction and RADAr. The second year has 45 EC compulsory religion-specific theory, research and applied coursework plus a 15-EC module/free-minor choice. This coherent route selects the first official listed Religie en Zorg module (three 5-EC courses). The third year has 5 EC compulsory humanities practice, a 10-EC required thesis, one selected 15-EC Worldviews, Climate and Nature module (first listed) and 30 EC of genuine free minor space. The university says students complete at least two thematic modules in the bachelor and have 30 EC of free minor space in total; this route has one module in each of years two and three, leaving two 15-EC free minor slots in year three. The year-three page displays multiple possible modules and two free-minor slots simultaneously as options; counting all as mandatory would exceed 60 EC. An alternative valid route may distribute module and free-minor credits differently. The 30-EC teaching minor is an optional instance of the free space, not a required teacher qualification.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target has no formal named specialization. One valid two-module route selects the first-listed year-two Religie en Zorg module and first-listed third-year Worldviews, Climate and Nature module; the 30-EC free minor space remains open. This neutral choice does not depend on UCR fit.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum is religious studies: a full first year studying Judaism, Islam, Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism, sacred texts, religious practices, theology, sociology and anthropology of religion; a further 45 EC of second-year work in philosophy of religious studies, spirituality, religious identity, migration, ritual and religious media; at least two 15-EC religion-based thematic modules; and an independent religion-politics-society final work. Even with the 30 EC genuinely free minor space, 150 EC remains in religious-studies and religion-linked practice, methods, modules and thesis. UCR lacks a dedicated course in the study of religion, religious traditions, theology or religion-specific research methods, let alone a coherent 24-course religious-studies progression. A programme in politics, philosophy and sociology could study surrounding social questions but would omit the target’s defining religion curriculum and would misrepresent a nearest academic match.
exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective pages reconcile to 180 EC when the two-module minimum is satisfied with a 15-EC module in year two and a 15-EC module in year three, while both 15-EC free minor slots occupy year three. Listed alternative modules and the optional teaching minor are choices, not additive compulsory courses. The exception rests on the missing religious-studies core, not on uncertainty about total credits or on a religious vocation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including name, description, outline-derived profile, prerequisites, planned terms and topics. GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly considers Buddhist approaches to self and consciousness, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature treat selected religiously inflected literary works, MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology and MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage encounter religious material culture, and GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law touches religious rights. GOSSOCI111/214/311, GOSPOLI111/112/212/311, GOSPHIL111/212 and GOSLAWJ111 support adjacent social, political and ethical inquiry. These are individual partial encounters or related disciplines; none teaches comparative religion, scriptures, religious traditions or methods of religious studies as a sustained curricular field. The workbook provides no basis for a defensible 24-course UCR programme that responds to this bachelor’s academic identity.
